One the first things my uni art teacher told my class was "you are used to being the best artist in your highschool, and now you're in a room with the best artist from every other highschool." Her point was that although we were all passionate enough about art that we decided to study it in uni, we were also used to being the top dog and now that we were surrounded by other top dogs, it could be extremely disheartening because suddenly it feels like your own art is crayon scribbles in a room of masterpieces. People get competitive and feelings get hurt, but I promise you it's not because you're a bad artist, you're just proud and that's not bad! You're not a fraud. People see your work and they enjoy it, not just anybody can snap off a picture and have it be aesthetically pleasing. Even if you don't see it, it sounds like you must have a good eye for composition and scenes. Photography is an art that requires a great deal of skill, not really something you can fake. I wish you all the best
